question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 5 \\ -5 & 4 & 5 \\ -5 & 2 & 7\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & a & 1 \\ 0 & b & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=PD{P}^{-1},$ find the value of $\frac{a}{b}.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that $D={P}^{-1}AP$ is a diagonalization of the matrix $A.$

From the diagonal matrix $D,$ we find that the eigenvalues of $A$ are

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=2\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}=4.$

The second column of $P$ corresponds to $\lambda =2.$ Computing $A-\lambda I,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 5 \\ -5 & 4 & 5 \\ -5 & 2 & 7\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 5 \\ -5 & 2 & 5 \\ -5 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 5 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & 5 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are free variables. From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Comparing this with the second column of $P,$ we deduce that ${x}_{3}=0.$ Now, setting ${x}_{2}=5$ and substituting our values for ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ into the general solution, we obtain the following: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{2}{5}.$
